stem.en: Which type of joint is mainly involved when you bend your knees and ankles?

text.en: Ball and socket joint, which lets the leg swing in a full circle.

feedback.en: No. The ball and socket joint of the leg is at the hip. The knee does not swing in a circle.

text.en: Hinge joint, which bends and straightens in one direction.

feedback.en: Yes. The knee bends and straightens in one direction only, like a door, so it is a hinge joint.

text.en: Pivot joint, which lets one bone turn from side to side on another.

feedback.en: No. The pivot joint is where the skull meets the backbone. The knee bends; it does not turn from side to side.

text.en: Fixed joint, which holds the bones still so that the leg stays firm.

feedback.en: No. Fixed joints join the bones of the skull and allow no movement. Your knees and ankles clearly move.

explanation.en: When you bend your knees and ankles, each one bends and straightens in a single direction. That is the movement of a hinge joint, the same type of joint as the elbow. The knee is a hinge joint protected by the kneecap.

hints.en: Bend your knee. Does it move in many directions or in one?
